newsitem.title: USA: Washington unaware if Mobutu has U.S. assets.
newsitem.headline: Washington unaware if Mobutu has U.S. assets.

text.p: The State Department said on Thursday it did not know if embattled Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko held any financial assets in the United States and had not been asked by Zairean rebels to take any action in the matter.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns also said Washington was not aware that Mobutu had personally embezzled any U.S. aid funds during his 30-year rule.

Zairean rebel representatives in Geneva said they wanted the United States, France and Belgium to freeze the assets of Mobutu, who appears on the point of being ousted by rebel forces. Switzerland has agreed to consider a similar request.
Mobutu is reported to hold overseas assets worth billions of dollars, but Burns told a news briefing: "We are just not aware of what his financial holdings may be here."

He said Washington had seen the reports from Geneva, but added: "Frankly, we've not been informed by the rebel alliance that they are expecting the United States to take any action in that regard. Perhaps it's directed at other countries."

Burns also said the United States was "not aware of any evidence of any diversion of U.S. assistance to Zaire to Mobutu's personal use", although it would be "extremely concerned" if there were such evidence.
The United States provided Zaire with substantial aid during the Cold War, when Mobutu was seen as an anti-communist bastion in Africa.
Burns dismissed the question of Mobutu's assets as "an issue for the government of Zaire to work out with the rebel alliance and others."
